Practices.Summary: HubSpot's testing practice is to use React Testing Library as its official UI testing framework, emphasizing user-focused tests over implementation details. The company migrated more than 76,000 tests from Enzyme to React Testing Library and runs frontend tests in the browser rather than JSDOM.

evidence.quote: in August of 2022, we announced Testing Library as our official UI testing framework and began our migration.
Over the next two and a half years, we migrated more than 76,000 tests from Enzyme to React Testing Library with virtually no automation.
Our frontend test setup is unique compared to much of the open source ecosystem in that we exclusively run our frontend tests in the browser.

Practices.Summary: HubSpot uses AI agents with hooks for testing validation, ensuring agents complete tasks only when builds pass and all changes are committed. AI fluency is now a baseline expectation for all engineering roles.

evidence.quote: Agents can be tamed. Claude Code (and other tools such as OpenCode) have support for hooks, which can be used to inject behavior at various points in the tool call lifecycle or before the agent stops.
Ensure the agent completes its task - block stopping until the build passes and all changes are committed and pushed to GitHub.
All HubSpot engineers leverage modern AI tools, and AI fluency is now a baseline expectation for all engineering roles.

evidence.quote: The last part involved ensuring compatibility with our existing public APIs. All our public APIs use Dropwizard's REST (JAX-RS) library, which makes it very easy to stand up new services.

Practices.Summary: HubSpot operates a massive Kubernetes-based CI/CD system running over 1 million builds per day across 3,000 EC2 instances hosting tens of thousands of microservices. For cloud coding agents, they use Kubernetes Jobs with 1:1 correspondence to agent executions, with custom Docker images containing Claude Code and developer tooling preinstalled.

evidence.quote: HubSpot already has an internal build and deploy system built on top of Kubernetes which runs over one million builds per day and hosts tens of thousands of microservices across approximately 3,000 EC2 instances.
Kubernetes Jobs - Agent executions correspond 1:1 with a Job resource in Kubernetes. The API server manages creating Jobs on-demand and monitors them for completion.

Docker images - We created custom Docker images with Claude Code and all of our other local developer tooling preinstalled. The image entrypoint handles cloning the Git repository targeted by the current execution and running Claude with the execution prompt.

Practices.Summary: HubSpot optimized build performance using dedicated Kubernetes node pools with build cache mounted from host, reducing first build times from 10-15 minutes to 2-3 minutes. The platform leverages enterprise-grade features like auto-scaling, observability, and region-aware API routing via Cloudflare Workers.

evidence.quote: Builds (especially Java builds) were extremely slow! To solve this, we used learnings from our internal build infrastructure and began running agents on a dedicated Kubernetes node pool with a build cache mounted from the host.
This reduced first build times for most repositories from 10-15 minutes to around 2-3 minutes.

By building on HubSpot's platform, we could leverage enterprise-grade CI/CD, auto-scaling, observability, and even region-aware API call routing built on Cloudflare Workers - all production ready features directly available to us without any additional setup.

Practices.Summary: HubSpot uses Sidekick AI code reviewer with Judge Agent quality gate to reduce time to first feedback by 90%, peaking at 99.76% reduction. The Judge Agent evaluates reviews for succinctness, accuracy, and actionability before posting to GitHub, maintaining high signal-to-noise ratio.

evidence.quote: Our AI code reviewer catches real issues, understands HubSpot-specific context, and maintains a high signal to noise ratio, often leaving no comments at all.
Sidekick has reduced the time it takes for engineers to get feedback on their code by 90%, peaking at a 99.76% reduction in September.
The Judge Agent acts as a quality gate between Sidekick's initial review and the comments that ultimately appear on a GitHub pull request.

After Sidekick drafts a review, the agent receives that output and evaluates it against three core criteria: Succinctness: Is the feedback clear and to the point? Accuracy: Is the suggestion technically correct within the context of the codebase and change? Actionability: If the feedback includes a code suggestion, can it be applied directly without additional modification?
Only review comments that pass the judge's evaluation are posted to GitHub, and everything else is filtered out.
AI pull request reviews are triggered automatically when pull requests are created, marked ready for review, or when Sidekick is manually requested as a reviewer

Over the past couple months, Sidekick has been rocking at an over 80% 'thumbs up' reaction rate, which we are very proud of.

Practices.Summary: HubSpot uses comprehensive dashboards to track debugging metrics including token usage, API costs, and failure counts per tool to identify optimization opportunities. Teams use cross-team embeds to provide white-glove migration services for large-scale migrations.

Practices.Summary: Engineers ensure AI agents handle errors gracefully through helpful error messages that allow models to self-correct. Common agent bugs included premature completion despite failing builds and forgetting to create pull requests.

evidence.quote: The model can still make mistakes. Ensure you return helpful errors to help the model correct itself.
Agents would often decide they were finished despite a failing build, not communicate adequately with users, or even entirely forget that they were supposed to create a pull request!

Practices.Summary: HubSpot intentionally uses short-lived access tokens decoupled from user identities for background data syncs, ensuring tokens only have required access scope.

evidence.quote: We intentionally avoided tying user identities to access tokens for background data syncs or automated workflows which don't expect user-level context during execution.
Because our access tokens are short-lived, we can safely assume that a token will only have the access that it should have.

Practices.Summary: HubSpot builds with small teams of 3-4 people where technical leaders are engineers first, managers second, staying hands-on with impactful work. Teams prioritize shipping quickly (hours to days) over perfect planning, with calculated risk-taking and low bureaucracy tolerance.

evidence.quote: We build with small teams of 3-4 people. Small teams with clear ownership can focus and move fast.

We only hire and promote technical engineering leaders. Our leaders prioritize solving for the customer over perfect processes, planning, or programs.
We favor starting small and learning quickly by shipping. Problems go from ideation to product in hours or days, not weeks.
